key_insight: Human body movements can be represented hierarchically as reusable atomic joint movements (Action Atoms) that temporally compose into higher-level patterns (Action Motifs); a nested latent Transformer (A4Mer) can discover this hierarchy in a fully self-supervised way from pose sequences.
problem_solved: Captures the compositional structure of human motion so that similar body-movement patterns are identified across different actions, improving efficiency, interpretability, and transferability of motion representations without requiring labeled data.
method: Define Action Atoms as short, atomic joint-movement units and Action Motifs as temporal compositions of these atoms that recur across actions.
Introduce A4Mer, a nested latent Transformer that models two hierarchical latent levels (atom-level and motif-level) and learns them jointly from pose sequences in a self-supervised manner.
Train with reconstruction/prediction-style objectives on unlabeled pose data so motifs emerge as shared, reusable building blocks for downstream tasks.
impact: Provides compact, interpretable, and transferable motion representations that improve downstream tasks (action recognition, prediction, synthesis) and reduce reliance on labeled data by leveraging compositionality.
visual_elements: Hierarchy diagram: skeleton → Action Atoms (short joint-movement clips) → Action Motifs (temporal composition) → full action
Model schematic: nested latent Transformer (atom-level encoder/decoder and motif-level aggregator) with data flow annotations
Cluster visualization: t-SNE/UMAP of motif embeddings showing motifs shared across different action labels
Sequence timeline: example skeleton frames with colored motif segments over time (showing motif reuse across actions)
paper_title: Action Motifs: Self-Supervised Hierarchical Representation of Human Body Movements
paper_authors: Genki Kinoshita, Shu Nakamura, Ryo Kawahara, Shohei Nobuhara, Yasutomo Kawanishi
